problem: The text calls A, B and C the three windings ("Join one end of each winding A, B and C to a common point N. Leave the other ends as the three line terminals"), but the star drawing uses A, B and C as the outer nodes joined to N, so it looks like A, B, C are the line terminals and there are no line terminals shown at all. A student comparing text and figure cannot tell where the three lines leave the star.
fix: Label the star drawing consistently with the text: draw three windings from line terminals L1, L2, L3 (the outer ends) to the common neutral N, and keep A, B, C as the winding names, so the star side shows both the line terminals and the neutral point, matching the delta side where D1, D2, D3 are marked.

problem: "Delta windings block zero-sequence current from the line side" is loosely worded. A delta winding does not block zero-sequence current; it gives zero-sequence current a closed path inside the triangle, so such current circulates in the delta and does not appear in the line conductors.
fix: Write: a delta winding gives zero-sequence current a closed path to circulate inside the triangle, so zero-sequence current does not appear in the line conductors; relays watch this circulating current.
